claims.text: Replacing TOR-TILD's classical EAM references with a high-temperature deep neural-network potential will significantly improve reference–target phase-space overlap in both solid and liquid states near melting.
The neural-network reference will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to current TOR-TILD EAM references.
The target materials are 3–5-component high-entropy alloys having 0–25 at.% of each principal element.
The intervention applies to both solid and liquid alloy states near their high melting temperatures.
A deep neural-network reference potential can be trained on ab initio configurations spanning solid and liquid high-temperature structures.
The reference potential should cover a broad range of alloy temperatures and compositions.
The applicable temperature interval is 0.9–1.1 times the melting temperature.
Using identical thermodynamic-integration protocols for the neural-network and EAM references permits a direct comparison.
The neural-network potential will enhance configurational sampling of local and global atomic environments.
Learning a representative ensemble of high-temperature configurations will increase overlap with the ab initio phase space.
Increased reference–target phase-space overlap will lower free-energy path differences.
Lower free-energy path differences will improve the accuracy of thermodynamic integration.
The neural-network reference will decrease mismatch with the ab initio target by at least tens of percent.
The neural-network approach will produce more accurate free-energy predictions than EAM references.
Existing TOR-TILD workflows use classical EAM reference potentials for solid–liquid near-melting free-energy calculations of high-entropy alloys.
The proposed method is applicable to 3–5-component metallic HEAs with no more than 25 at.% of each element.
The method may become less effective at lower temperatures or for compositions outside the training set.
The degree of improvement depends on training-set quality, training-set diversity, and ab initio data fidelity.

contradictions.description: If the stated 0–25 at.% range applies to every element in the complete alloy, a three-component composition cannot sum to 100 at.%, and a four-component composition can do so only when every element is exactly 25 at.%.

The prediction calls for a decrease of at least tens of percent, whereas the falsification rule rejects the hypothesis only when there is no reduction. A small reduction would fail the stated prediction without satisfying the stated falsification condition.
